# Vantorre kickoff

2025-07-15

Kickoff with Mateo Quiroga and the Vantorre Group procurement and Hartford operations team. Agreed sequence: Hartford first; Albany in Q4. Keep the initial Pemberline Dock setup focused on Hartford receiving rather than bringing both sites into the same working session.

**Discussion**
- Hartford’s morning inbound queue is the immediate pain point. Drivers arriving before the receiving desk opens; appointment details then copied from email into the shift spreadsheet.
- Operations walked through doors 3 and 4, where pallet deliveries overlap with returns collection. Need separate appointment labels so the desk can distinguish unloading from pickup without opening every booking.
- Mateo asked for one clear view of the day’s exceptions: late arrivals, missing references, and loads moved between doors. A printable “Hartford Daily Exceptions” report would help the afternoon handover.
- Procurement wants supplier booking instructions reviewed before distribution. Current draft says “delivery reference,” while Hartford staff use “PO reference”; settle the wording before the walkthrough.
- Albany discussion deliberately brief. Q4 remains the next phase; capture differences in receiving hours and door naming during the Hartford work.
- Small snag in the sample upload: two rows used the same refernce. Operations will send a cleaned file.

**Actions**
- I’ll circulate the Hartford walkthrough agenda and revised booking instructions.
- Mateo to gather procurement comments into one reply.
- Hartford operations to send the door list, receiving hours, and corrected sample file.
- Add Albany requirements to the Q4 preparation list.

# Coastal pipeline review

**Meeting date:** Thursday, 30 Oct 2025  
**Meeting:** Coastal pipeline call  
**Attendees:** Bettina Kroll, Sofia Marchetti, Kwame Adjei-Rowe, June Osei-Lark

## Summary

The call focused on operational blockers affecting the Coastal pipeline. Discussion stayed with scheduling workflows, buyer follow-up and materials needed for the next conversations. No pricing decisions were made during the call.

Bettina asked that the next round of demonstrations use customer-specific arrival patterns rather than the standard sample yard. June will review the resulting proposal language for consistency with what Pemberline Dock actually supports.

## Account discussion

### Pellucid Harbor Logistics

- The dispatch team wants a clearer view of trucks arriving before their assigned windows. In the walkthrough, an early arrival at door 6 appeared beside an on-time appointment without enough visual distinction for the gate clerk.
- The next demonstration should include a Gulf Coast morning sequence: overnight arrivals, a shift handover and two trailers competing for the same unload window.
- Bettina will obtain a redacted dispatch sheet so the team can reproduce the sequence without using driver phone numbers.

### Driftmoor Marine Freight

- Kwame described a mismatch between the barge arrival board and the dock appointment view. The operations contact wants to hold a tentative unloading slot while the vessel arrival remains subject to change.
- Bettina asked, “Can we use Kwame's port account to test the tentative-slot walkthrough before the next coastal demo?”
- The group agreed to show the distinction between a provisional appointment and a committed door assignment, including what the afternoon dispatcher sees when the arrival moves.
- Kwame will send the current screen sequence and the specific point where dispatch loses track of the revised time.

### Saltmarsh Provisions

- Corinne Ashdown wants the receiving supervisor to see late inbound loads before allocating the next wave of grocery deliveries.
- The proposed demonstration will follow a chilled load arriving at door 3 during the early shift, with a delayed unload pushing the following appointment.
- Bettina will ask Corinne Ashdown whether the supervisor works primarily from the appointment board or an exported receiving report.

### Covey & Lark Retail

- The warehouse team requested a simpler explanation of how rescheduling affects the door view. The last walkthrough moved too quickly between the yard queue and appointment details.
- I will prepare a shorter sequence using one inbound home-goods trailer, one occupied door and a single reschedule.

## Action items

- **Bettina:** Collect the dispatch example and confirm the Saltmarsh Provisions demonstration workflow.
- **Kwame:** Send the revised-arrival screen sequence.
- **Sofia:** Rework the Covey & Lark Retail walkthrough.
- **June:** Review proposal wording after the demonstration outlines are circulated.

calendar.title: Intro: Orlavene Health
calendar.notes:
# Intro: Orlavene Health

February 11, 2026

Intro call. Orlavene Health, hospital group in Denver. Prospect, not a customer. No signed agreement. Mostly receiving-team questions; less interest in the yard map than I expected.

Orlavene described the morning pinch at the central receiving dock: linen truck, food delivery, then medical supplies all arriving around shift change. Door 2 gets treated as the overflow door, except nobody tells the driver when the assignment changes. Driver waits outside, receiving calls security, security calls receiving. Lots of phone tag.

Walked through Pemberline Dock. Appointment board first, then door assignment and arrival status. They wanted to see what a receiving clerk actually clicks with a truck already waiting. Skipped the broader overview. Used a sample food-service delivery; moved it from Door 1 to Door 2 and showed the updated board.

Orlavene asked about deliveries that arrive without an appointment. Also whether the afternoon team could see why a morning booking moved. Need a tighter follow-up demo around those two situations, not another tour of every screen.

Pricing question came late. Explained per seat per year. No numbers discussed. They need to work out who would use it: receiving desk, shift leads, possibly security. Not everyone who gets a delivery notification.

Name looks close to Orlavine Medical Supply. Different company. Keep Orlavene Health on the invite.

## Actions

- Send recap and ask for a sample receiving schedule.
- Build demo: unplanned arrival, door change, afternoon handoff.
- Ask Orlavene which receiving staff should join the next call.

mail.subject: Re: missed barge slot notifications
mail.body:
Looping in Support + Bettina. Driftmoor Marine Freight escalated yesterday, Aug 26th. Barge slot notifications not sent. Dispatch had the bookings in Pemberline Dock, but nobody on the evening crew got the notices they use to line up trucks for the ramp.

Need someone on the delivery trail this morning, pls. Not just whether the booking saved.

They checked junk folders while we were on the phone. Nothing there either. One driver was already waiting by the weighbridge when the ramp clerk found the revised slot on screen.

I've asked them to leave the affected bookings alone for now. No deleting/recreating to see if that wakes it up. They have screenshots of the slot history and can send the original export rather than another cropped picture.

Support — can you pull notification creation, queue and delivery events for those three bookings? Also check whether the slot-change action is being recorded separately from the send. Ticket PS-4826 has the booking refs; putting them there rather than scattering them across this thread.

For today dispatch is phoning the ramp clerk after each change. Clunky, but at least someone is reading it back. Need to know if other notification types are affected before telling them that workaround covers everything.

Will chase the export now. Sorry, typing between calls — the screenshot attachment didnt come through first time.
